text.p: These are some of the main stories in Sofia newspapers today. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-- Bulgaria's cabinet is planning to launch a programme to crack down on drug and fire weapon smuggling and illegal migration, Prime Minister Ivan Kostov said.
-- Bulgaria's government is expected to conduct tests to evaluate the competence of state administration officials, deputy Prime minister Veselin Metodiev said. @
-- Bulgaria's state carrier Balkan Airlines said it expected to receive an offer from Boeing by end-August for new aircraft to replace Balkan's ageing Soviet-made airplanes.
-- Bulgaria expects to attract some $800 million foreign investments by the end of this year, Foreign Investment Agency executive director Iliyan Vassilev said.
-- Bulgaria's broad money rose by 223 billion levs in the second week of July to 4.492 trillion levs, Bulgarian National Bank figures showed.

-- Lev-denominated deposits in Bulgarian commercial banks rose to 635.5 billion levs from 520.9 billion levs in the first two weeks of July as Bulgarians sold marks for levs after the country introduced a currency board system on July 1, Bulgarian National Bank figures showed.

-- Bulgarian commercial banks will have to register 10 billion levs capital by the end of 1998 to meet minimum capital requirements under the new Banking Law approved by parliament earlier last month, the Bulgarian National Bank said.

-- Bulgaria is expected to lift the ban on purchases of real estate property in the country by foreigners, Foreign Investment Agency executive director Iliyan Vassilev said. -- Sofia Newsroom, (++359-2) 981 8569
